answer: The willow test I would run is Watchmaker dial standard stamped by the observatory register: each dial is a calibration record countersigned by the assay office, so a farm must assemble a hundred real watches by hand, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the copper of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out. The quartz is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
